clue.text: Stew fruit for Spooner's classically trained actor

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words found are exchanged at their starts

explanation.surface: Someone stews a fruit, offered up for a stage performer.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of COOK MELON gives roughly 'Mook Kellon', which is close to the actor's name; the blog calls it a loose Spoonerism.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Ian McKellen is an English actor with a long Shakespearean stage career, hence classically trained.

clue.text: Lose machine pistol, unfortunately abandoning hit on rogue

indicators.note: unfortunately signals the letters are shuffled into an unlucky new order
abandoning tells us some letters are left behind out of the fodder
rogue means wayward, so the letters of hit on may be in any order

explanation.surface: A gunman loses a machine pistol after failing to hit a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of HIT ON out of MACHINE PISTOL and rearrange the eight that remain.
explanation.definitionFit: To misplace something is to put it somewhere forgotten, which amounts to losing it.

clue.text: Furore over contracts

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned over means read upwards

parts.note: to cause a stink = to kick up a furore

explanation.surface: An uproar about some contracts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracts' looks like a noun about deals, but it is a verb, as brows do when a person frowns.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb sense: brows that knit draw together, so knitting is a kind of contracting.

clue.text: Exposed figure in trouble climbing coastal region

indicators.note: in means the second group of letters sits within the first
in a down clue climbing means the word reads upwards, from bottom to top
exposed means stripped of its outer covering, so the first and last letters go

explanation.surface: A figure is caught exposed while in trouble climbing along a coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exposed' reads like a description of the figure, but it strips the word's outer letters; 'climbing' works because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Liguria is the region of north-west Italy along the Mediterranean, including Genoa and the Riviera.

clue.text: Head of college dropped for real

indicators.note: in a down clue, the top letter drops to the bottom

parts.note: a tech is a technical college; TECH less its head
the T at the top of TECH moves to the foot

explanation.surface: A college principal genuinely demoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of college' reads as a principal; it is only the first letter of the college, which falls to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A borrowing from German, where echt means genuine, used in English for authentic things.

clue.text: Whacked and remains in bunk

indicators.note: the remains go inside the bunk

parts.note: a bunk is a BED; its first letter, before the remains
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: Someone beaten and lying dead in a bunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' suggests a body; it is what is left after a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are informal past tenses for striking something hard.

clue.text: Opposite some army, not natives retreating

indicators.note: the part is read backwards
only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: Facing part of an army of foreign troops in retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: The military picture of an army retreating hides a word for 'opposite' read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun sense: in grammar an opposite is a word meaning the reverse of another, like hot for cold.

clue.text: With post in support, present other side

indicators.note: in a down clue, the post sits beneath and holds up the other part

parts.note: present = here, as at a roll call

explanation.surface: A job applicant holding a post while showing their other side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' is the Latin prefix for after, not a job or a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'the other side' is a euphemism for life after death, which is what the word names.

clue.text: One moving quickly turned down that woman

indicators.note: the word for down is turned back to front

explanation.surface: A quick mover who rejected a particular woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned down' reads as rejected; split it into 'turned' as the instruction and 'down' as the mood.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent noun: someone who dashes is moving quickly, as Santa's reindeer Dasher does.

clue.text: Weapon left in grass ruined

explanation.surface: A weapon left lying in the grass, now spoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is British slang for informing to the police, so it is a verb, not the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a slingshot, or catapult, is a simple hand weapon for flinging stones.

clue.text: Teaching in France, you tinker with course, ultimately getting demoted

indicators.note: in a down clue, the letter moves lower down the entry
the word for you is the French one

parts.note: a TOERAG is a scoundrel or tramp, as a tinker was; its E is pulled out

indicators.note: the last letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the E, last letter of coursE, drops to the bottom

explanation.surface: A French pupil fiddling with their course and being moved down a class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tinker' is the noun, an old insult for a travelling mender, like the British toerag, not the verb fiddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal noun: tutorage is the work or office of a tutor, so teaching.

clue.text: Picked up car parts — exhausts

indicators.note: picked up by the ear: heard

parts.note: tyres, British spelling of the rubber on car wheels

explanation.surface: Someone collects car parts, including exhaust pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhausts' looks like car parts too, but it is the verb: wears out.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a long walk tires or exhausts you.

clue.text: Desire tips from actor Charlie Sheen

indicators.note: the tips here are the final letters

explanation.surface: An actor's desires, with the name Charlie Sheen as the punchline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Actor Charlie Sheen' is a single famous name, but the definition is only the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: polished wood has a soft shine, a sheen.

clue.text: Primitive prudent to muffle sound

indicators.note: the word for prudent wraps round the sound, as a muffler wraps round a noise

parts.note: sage = wise, prudent; split after its first letter

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned person careful to keep the noise down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primitive' reads as a noun for a person, but the answer is an adjective, hence the hyphen.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: anything crude or outdated is called stone-age, after the era of stone tools.

clue.text: Propose moving radioactive waste once mutated wisteria removed

indicators.note: moving suggests the letters shift about into a new order
removed tells us a set of letters is taken out of the fodder
once mutated means after being changed in form, so the plant's letters may come in any order

explanation.surface: Nuclear waste is said to have mutated a climbing plant, now dug out.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike the letters of WISTERIA from RADIOACTIVE WASTE and rearrange the rest; 'once' just joins the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate a plan is to recommend it publicly, which is to put it forward or propose it.

clue.text: Bid in good time for computer application

explanation.surface: An auction bid lodged in good time for some software.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bid' suggests an auction; it is the old verb meaning order, as in 'do as you are bid'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Windows program where users type text instructions goes by this name.

clue.text: Interdependence of lifting corporation with excellence leader overlooked

indicators.note: in a down clue, the word is read upwards
the first letter is left out

parts.note: a corporation is jokingly a pot belly, a TUM, read upwards

explanation.surface: Business jargon about a rising corporation depending on excellence under a neglectful boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' is old slang for a large belly, so the business picture is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a relationship of mutual dependence is one where each side relies on the other.

clue.text: Backing old American in China pursuing contract rivals

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so this part follows the first

parts.note: in contract bridge East and South sit at adjacent seats and are opponents

indicators.note: in means these letters sit within the word for a friend

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal

explanation.surface: An elderly American in China is chasing business rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: China plate is rhyming slang for mate, hence PAL; ES are two opposing seats at a bridge table.
explanation.definitionFit: Espousal is the adoption or support of a cause, so it is a synonym of backing.

clue.text: Ways of hiding nauseous reaction being imprisoned by two deities

indicators.note: OF holds the reaction inside it
the result is locked between the two gods

parts.note: OF from the clue, split round the reaction

explanation.surface: Methods of concealing queasiness while locked up by a pair of gods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' looks like a link word joining 'Ways' to the rest, but it is wordplay material.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a main road is a public way, and roads are often called ways in street names.

clue.text: The devil among us?

definitions.note: 'the devil' works as an intensifier in a question, not as a noun
definitions.meaning: the emphatic phrase in 'what the devil is going on?'
here in the world of the living

explanation.surface: A suggestion that Satan walks among ordinary people.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the trick: 'the devil' is not Satan but the phrase that adds force to 'what the devil?', which can be swapped for 'what on earth?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an intensifier in questions, and a phrase for being in this world among the living.

clue.text: Using every effort, disregard entertaining act on vacation

indicators.note: the word for disregard hosts the other part

parts.note: to flout a rule = to disregard it; FLOUT split round the act

indicators.note: act is vacated, emptied of its middle

explanation.surface: Working all out while ignoring a holiday entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' suggests a holiday; here it means emptied, keeping only the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: working flat out means at full speed, with every effort.

clue.text: A time to wear gym shoes, according to some, changes

indicators.note: the time is worn inside the shoes

parts.note: daps is a regional word for plimsolls; DAPS split before its last letter

explanation.surface: Some people claim a certain time demands gym shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'According to some' flags a regional word: in Wales and the West of England, plimsolls (canvas gym shoes) are daps.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to adjust something for a new use is to alter it.

clue.text: Drug chart reviewed following one entering stupor

indicators.note: following means this part comes after the other
entering means the numeral goes into the word for stupor

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: reviewed is taken as re-viewed, looked at the other way, so read backwards

explanation.surface: A patient's drug chart is checked again after someone slips into a stupor.
explanation.definitionFit: Diazepam, sold as Valium, is a sedative medicine prescribed for anxiety.

clue.text: Tailless monkey covers metres to get to grass

parts.note: a BABOON is a monkey; lose the N and split round the metres

explanation.surface: A monkey without a tail stretching metres to reach the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' sounds like a lawn, but botanically the giant woody plant belongs to the grass family, so the definition is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical fact: this tall woody plant is a member of the grass family.

clue.text: Be niggled regularly lacking shade

indicators.note: every other letter is missing

parts.note: nIgGlEd, keeping the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Irritated by always being in the sun without shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be' is used as it stands, and 'regularly lacking' keeps the alternate letters of 'niggled'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this pale sandy colour is one shade among many.

clue.text: Writer of superb I, Robot

indicators.note: the answer is made of part of the following words

explanation.surface: An author of the superb novel I, Robot.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at Isaac Asimov; the writer is a thing that writes, and Biro is the British name for a ballpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: a pen is literally a writer, and in Britain any ballpoint is called by this brand name.

clue.text: Told nosey parker earlier

indicators.note: spoken, so the answer is heard

parts.note: a pryer is one who pries into other people's business

explanation.surface: Someone warned a busybody ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: A nosey parker is British slang for a busybody.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a prior engagement is one arranged earlier than this one.

clue.text: Models I twice separately encountered in record books

indicators.note: each I is met inside a part of the record books

parts.note: tomes are large books; TOMES split round the second I

explanation.surface: Supermodels appearing twice in the record books.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual plural drops the second I, and the paper later apologised for the spelling; the wordplay still builds this form.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a perfect example of a type serves as a model of it.

clue.text: Bladed tool hurt — article put aside for year

indicators.note: put aside for means one letter is set aside and another takes its place

parts.note: scathe is an old word meaning to hurt or harm

explanation.surface: Someone hurt by a sharp tool sets the article aside for a year.
explanation.walkthrough: SCATHE is archaic for harm, the root of 'unscathed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scythe is a long curved blade on a pole, used for cutting grass by hand.

clue.text: Nut clamping to wheel oddly in vehicle recess

indicators.note: the nut grips the other letters inside it

parts.note: a nut is a FOOL, split round the wheel letters

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are kept

explanation.surface: A loose nut tightened onto a wheel in a car's recess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' looks like a bolt fitting in a car picture, but it is a person, a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A compound: the recess in a car's floor is the well where the driver's feet go.
